explainer_content.short_definition: The late-1960s heavy guitar road where blues-rock, psychedelia, distortion, and extended soloing push toward hard rock and metal.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Hendrix, Cream, The Doors, Steppenwolf, and related bands took the blues-rock base of the British Invasion and made it louder, darker, and more exploratory. The sound can be riff-heavy, organ-haunted, feedback-soaked, or jam-driven, but it usually keeps a blues pulse under the psychedelic surface.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It is one of the clearest bridges from 1960s pop-rock into 1970s hard rock, heavy metal, and arena guitar identity.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: Compared with psychedelic pop, it is less cute and less compact. Compared with hard rock, it is more exploratory and acid-colored.
what_to_listen_for: Organ or studio effects adding darkness
Riffs that feel heavier than the song form around them
